headline: UKMTO reports a NEW tanker struck by 'unknown projectile' 11nm off Bukha (Khasab), Oman on Oct 21
dek: A tanker 11nm off Bukha, Oman was struck by an unknown projectile on Oct 21, sparking a fire; vessel now at anchor, all crew safe. A second incident (Oct 20) saw a projectile hit a tanker 30nm off Al Faw, Iraq with no casualties.
fault_line: Who is hitting the tankers — Iranian mines or US/covert sabotage — and does the new Oman strike change the rules of engagement before a third US carrier arrives?

sections.what_happened: A tanker 11nm off Bukha, Oman was struck by an unknown projectile on Oct 21, sparking a fire; vessel now at anchor, all crew safe. A second incident (Oct 20) saw a projectile hit a tanker 30nm off Al Faw, Iraq with no casualties.
sections.what_verified: UKMTO primary; relayed by Gulf News live blog (citing AP) and Economic Times within hours. Separately, Reuters counted 18 vessel attacks in 2 weeks (Kpler, covered 1500-04).
sections.what_disputed: IRGC/Sepah News (Xinhua relay) claims these were ships striking Iranian mines on an 'illegal' route — contradicts UKMTO projectile framing; no independent verification of who struck.
sections.why_matters: The Hormuz tanker war just moved to Oman's side of the strait — UK maritime agency confirms a NEW projectile strike while Tehran calls it mine justice. 20% of the world's oil now transits a live firing zone.
sections.context: Background: Hormuz — UKMTO reports a NEW tanker struck by 'unknown projectile' 11nm off Bukha (Khasab), Oman on Oct 21 (fire, now at anchor, crew safe, no environmental impact); UKMTO also logged a second incident Tuesday 30nm off Al Faw, Iraq (no casualties/damage). Context: IRGC claims two tankers hit naval mines (Oct 20 statement, covered); Gulf News live blog 15:19 + Economic Times 15:26 carry the UKMTO alerts. Follows CENTCOM naming five destroyed Iranian tankers (1300-01).

totw_analysis: Our read: The Hormuz tanker war just moved to Oman's side of the strait — UK maritime agency confirms a NEW projectile strike while Tehran calls it mine justice. 20% of the world's oil now transits a live firing zone. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Who is hitting the tankers — Iranian mines or US/covert sabotage — and does the new Oman strike change the rules of engagement before a third US carrier arrives?
